audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Neeko / Skill / Skill, which disagrees with the packet chart, with the mirror audit, and with the page's own prose — whys[1] through whys[5] describe Nautilus dictating every trade, and spikes[2] explicitly calls Level 6 muted for Neeko while the chart hands her that row.
audit.why: Dredge Line (1150 range, 14/13/12/11/10s) plus the Staggering Blow passive root and Riptide (7/6.5/6/5.5/5s) is a full CC chain the moment he has two points, and Titan's Wrath shields the answer. Neeko has no way to punish that until Liandry's-class items let her poke from outside 1150.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill, Levels 2 through first item Nautilus, 2+ items Neeko — matched full+content pairs with ratings moved to match.

audit.why: The mirror recorded spikes as unchanged and the four entries here are right: Neeko's Level 1 range edge, his Level 3-5 hook window, the muted Level 6, and her 2+ item takeover. This is also the matchup's real story — the 57.89% win rate is earned after items, not in lane.
audit.corrected: No spike-timing changes; realigned full:phases[N].why so the level chart tells the same story the spikes do.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] says Depth Charge keeps his kill threat 'in a point-blank fight'. Depth Charge is an 825-range shockwave that chases its target across that distance — he never has to be point-blank. Separately, tradeBad, dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d are boilerplate about 'a mobile champion' and 'whiffing it into a dash', which describes neither Nautilus nor the actual losing play here, and dosFull[0].d says 'count it' without ever giving the number to count.
audit.why: Telling the player the threat is point-blank invites them to ult at the edge of their 600 radius and feel safe; the charge covers 825 and knocks up en route. And the genuine trap in this lane is spending Tangle-Barbs as poke — the content layer already says so, while the full layer's don'ts say something else entirely.
audit.corrected: Depth Charge reaches 825 and travels to you, so distance alone is not the answer — the travel is the tell. Dredge Line is 1150 range on a 14s cooldown at rank 1: that count is the whole green-light system. Hold Tangle-Barbs (12s at rank 1) as the anti-hook, never as poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: The most punishable cooldown in the lane — Dredge Line at 14s rank 1 — is named everywhere and numbered nowhere.
audit.why: 'Bait it, count it, then go' is unusable without the number; a 14s window is a whole trade and a wave crash, a 10s one at rank 5 is not.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to dosFull[0].d and to the level-2 and 2+ items chart rows.

notes: UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: four strings (whys[4] before my edit, spikes[2].text, mid, wants.foe[2]) claim Depth Charge's knockup interrupts Pop Blossom's wind-up. Riot's text calls the wind-up 'a short preparation' and carries no channel flag, and interrupt eligibility is exactly the class of fact the kit files cannot settle. I corrected only the part I could verify — the 825 range and the chase, against the 'point-blank' claim — and left the interrupt assertion standing rather than guess in either direction. Worth one confirmation pass. DIFFICULTY: left at EVEN 5.5/10. The mirror set Nautilus's side to EVEN 6/10, whose inverse would be nearer 4/10 here, but a 57.89% win rate that arrives entirely after two items does not read as an easy lane; mirror-fix.js can arbitrate. Packet defect note claims the chart is wrong because Neeko wins 57.89% — that is the same reasoning I rejected on mordekaiser: she loses the lane and wins the game, which is what spikes[3] says.
